'''Rose Whelan Sedgewick''' ({{circa|1904}} – 2000) was an American [[mathematician]]. She was the first person to earn a PhD in mathematics from [[Brown University]], in 1929.<ref name=BAM>{{cite news|title=Obituaries|url=http://www.brownalumnimagazine.com/content/view/1577/40/|access-date=4 December 2013|newspaper=Brown Alumni Magazine|date=September–October 2000}}</ref> Her subsequent career in mathematics included assistant professorships at the University of Rochester, the University of Connecticut, Hillyer College, and the University of Maryland.<ref name=StPetersburg>{{cite news|title=St. Petersburg Times Obituaries|url=http://www.sptimes.com/Archive/061300/Obits.shtml|access-date=3 December 2013|newspaper=St. Petersburg Times|date=13 June 2000}}</ref>

Sedgewick is the namesake of the Rose Whelan Society at Brown, an organization for women and gender minorities who are graduate students, post-doctoral fellows and faculty in pure and applied in mathematics.<ref name=WhelanSociety>{{cite web |title=The Rose Whelan Society |url=https://www.math.brown.edu/rosewhelan |publisher=Department of Mathematics, Brown University |access-date=13 August 2022}}</ref> She was married to fellow mathematician Charles H.W. Sedgewick and had four children.<ref name=Green>{{cite book| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|year=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Society|page=68|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics |contribution=Sedgewick, Rose Whelan|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jUrq3bUvQlYC&pg=PA68 |access-date=4 December 2013|isbn=9780821896747}} Biography on p.548-551 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref> She died on June 7, 2000, at the age of 96.<ref name=StPetersburg />
